#886. Alanis Morissette Comes Out as Pansexual

Alanis Morissette—who shares kids Ever, 14, Onyx, 9, and Winter, 6, with husband Mario "Souleye" Treadway—shared that she identifies as pansexual: “I like to leave it for the epilogue.”

Alanis Morissette thinks you oughta know a bit more about her personal life.

After Fortune Feimster asked the Grammy winner if the men who inspired her breakup songs ever made her think about swinging a different way, Morissette dispelled precious illusions about her sexuality, sharing she identifies as pansexual.

“I’m sorry for the men that hurt you, but I’m not sorry for the songs that came from it,” Feimster told Morissette on a recent episode of her, Tig Notaro and Mae Martin’s Handsome Podcast. “Did it make you want to be a lesbian at any point?”

As the “You Oughta Know” singer replied, “I’m pansexual, so, yeah.”

Surprised by Morissette’s admission that she’s attracted to all sexes, Notaro chimed in “Wait, you’re not really pansexual, are you?” to which the “Ironic” singer confirmed, “I am.”

When Notaro joked that the “You Learn” singer should have started the podcast with the confession, Morissette joked, “I like to leave it for the epilogue.”

“I like to confuse people on the way out,” she quipped. “Is it confusing?”

But it wouldn’t be the only time the 52-year-old—who shares kids Ever, 14, Onyx, 9, and Winter, 6, with husband Mario "Souleye" Treadway—has pulled her hand out of her pocket when it comes to her private life.

After all, Morissette made a sweet confession about the fulfillment motherhood has given her while getting inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame, sharing the role is by far her most prestigious honor.

“Archetypically, ‘Mom’ is number one for me,” she told E! News ahead of the ceremony at the Marriott Maquis in New York June 11, “and ‘writer’ is number two, so for that to be marked tonight, it really warms my heart.”

And while Morissette considers family her crowning achievement, she also shared how much it meant to receive acclaim after inspiring a new generation of writers.

“Any of us writers, women, non-gendered, binary identifying, men frankly,” she continued. “There’s a lot of men who I connect with on this level. I think it’s those of us who are very sensitive and those of us who are empaths, we unite in a very quiet introverted way, and a lot of writers are introverts.”

But Morissette has a lot to say “thank U” for as of late. After all, she just began her Inglewood residency Butterfly With a Machete Nov. 5.

“The ‘90s message for me was basically stay in one lane as though that’s even possible for a whole human being,” she explained. “So this musical show, piece—I don’t even know what to call it. It’s a trauma-edy.”

As she noted, “It’s taking all the challenges and some of the stories of my life and transmuting it into dance or movement or stories, comedy—and always music. Music’s number one.”

But Morissette isn’t the only star to open up about her sexuality. Keep reading for more stars who have done the same...

The Dance Moms alum didn't give it a second thought when she came out in a 2021 Instagram story.

"I came out when I was 17 but I didn't understand at the time what a big deal that was," she told People in October 2023. "I didn't understand why that was scary."

"Of course there was a lot of positivity and love and acceptance but then there was a lot of negativity, and I did lose a lot," she continued. "I didn't care, and I still don't care [about] the things I lost and the people that I lost and if I lost a chunk of fans...because it's who I am."

While the "Flowers" singer was never a big fan of labels, she came out as pansexual in 2016.

"My whole life, I didn't understand my own gender and my own sexuality," she revealed to Variety in October 2016. "I always hated the word 'bisexual,' because that's even putting me in a box. I don't ever think about someone being a boy or someone being a girl."

She continued, "Also, my nipple pasties and s--t never felt sexualized to me. My eyes started opening in the fifth or sixth grade. My first relationship in my life was with a chick."

For Matt, coming out to his conservative Christian family marked the start of a new era in his life.

"Telling your family is a huge, huge deal," the White Collar alum, who shares three kids with husband Simon Halls, previously told OUT Magazine. "I really view my life as divided between the time before I told my parents, and the time after. And the decisions I made, and the life I lived, before and after, are vastly different. It's night and day."

The "Good Luck, Babe!" singer revealed that she isn't always as confident and comfortable as she may seem. And her Midwest roots played a huge role.

"I was scared of flamboyantly gay people because I was taught that," she told Rolling Stone. "[I realized] people hate flamboyantly gay people because it just exudes femininity, and people hate women. Just little things like that, you're like, 'Oh my God, this is just so f--ked.'"

"It took a lot of unlearning, and there's still things I"m still confused about, and [it's] why I feel so uncomfortable being gay sometimes," she continued. "I don't get why this is such an issue for me. It shouldn't be, but something's just going on and I need to just accept that."

The Bachelorette alum came out on an episode of The View, when she revealed she was in a committed relationship with Robby Hoffman, the comedian she wed in January 2025.

"I've been keeping it kind of private," she said in the August 2023 episode, "because it is a bigger story and a bigger conversation because I'm dating a girl."

"I think it was always a whisper in me that just got louder and louder," she continued. "I didn't really know to pay attention to it. When this happens there's some shame attached to it and I had to a little bit navigate through that shame; what is it, where is it coming from."

The Mean Girls star, having previously identified as bisexual, came out as lesbian in January 2024—on an episode of Saturday Night Live. And her friends played a supporting role in the decision.

“All of a sudden, I had these people around me who were either nonbinary people, trans friends, or lesbians," she told Billboard months later, "and I was like, ‘I feel so happy when I’m with you guys. And I also really want to call myself a lesbian when I’m around you.’”

The former late-night host officially came out as queer on the last day of Pride month in 2024.

“In what will come as a shock to exactly zero people, I’m using the last day of PRIDE to come out!” she wrote in a June 2024 Instagram post, wearing a tank with the word “Queer” printed on the front.

“Be proud of who you are, little babies! I know I am!” she continued. “And I can’t wait to be discriminated against for a new reason!!”

Before revealing her sexuality, the former Disney Channel star was actually nervous to publicly come out as queer.

"I've hinted about my sexuality for years while being afraid to spell it out for everybody," she told Gay Times in May 2021. "I did a lyric video last year, for 'We Belong.' It had moving line drawings of people falling in love…It was all a man and a woman making out and it was a weird moment for me."

"When the song came out, everybody got the idea that the song was a big LGBTQ+ anthem song and I found myself in this position where everyone thought I was queerbaiting," she continued. "I went on Instagram Live and said 'Guys, I really needed to explain something to you. Maybe I haven't said it, but I'm super queer. This is something I want to represent through my music because it's who I am.'"

The "Heart Attack" singer came out as nonbinary in a 2021 Instagram post.

"Every day we wake up, we are given another opportunity and chance to be who we want and wish to be," she wrote in the caption. "I've spent the majority of my life growing in front of all of you… you've seen the good, the bad, and everything in between. Not only has my life been a journey for myself, I was also living for those on the other side of the cameras."

"Today is a day I'm so happy to share more of my life with you all - I am proud to let you know that I identify as non-binary and will officially be changing my pronouns to they/them moving forward," Demi—who has since gone back to using she/her pronouns—continued. "This has come after a lot of healing and self-reflective work. I'm still learning and coming into myself, and I don't claim to be an expert or a spokesperson. Sharing this with you now opens another level of vulnerability for me."

Though the Bachelor alum has been dating singer Hayley Kiyoko since 2018, she did not publicly come out until four years into her relationship. And though she admitted it felt weird once everyone found out, she saw the impact of publicly sharing her truth.

"I realized this is so much bigger than me and my relationship and my personal experience because if it helped anyone feel comfortable or brave to be comfortable with who they fall in love with, then that's way bigger than me and my fears and what I was scared of," she told E! News in June 2022. "It's very humbling to read comments like that and realize the significance of something as simple as falling in love and sharing that."

Three years after coming out to his family at age 15, Troye publicly shared his story in a YouTube video. And as he later recalled, his decision to come out occurred amid a pivotal moment in his life.

"I was about to sign my record deal, and I really wanted to be in charge of how I came out," he told People in February 2022. "I didn't want anyone to take that away from me. I wanted to start going out and going to gay clubs and meeting boys, and I wanted to write songs about love that were true and genuine."

The Selling Sunset star—who is married to singer G Flip—stresses the importance of prioritizing yourself.

"If someone truly loves you, your happiness should always come before their beliefs," Chrishell, who began her romance with the Australian singer in 2022, told E! News. "Never conform to others ideas they have for your life. It's yours and you only get one."

The TikToker—who was openly gay at an all-boys high school—uses his platform to encourage others to be comfortable with who they are.

"My identity will already be something that can be of controversy, depending on who the audience is," Chris told E! News in October 2022. "So one of my passive-active missions in having this platform is to try to break that down and bring normalcy to this identity."

The Bravo star, who came out while in college, shared some valuable advice for having those big coming out conversations.

"My advice would be, find one friend that you can tell," he previously told E! News. "All it takes is one friend that you know will be supportive. And that friend can be your island and just kind of branch out from there. It's always worse in your head than it's going to be."

The MCU’s Multiverse Saga is nearly over, but there are plenty more Marvel movies and shows on the horizon.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Marvel fatigue? Think again, especially after Spider-Man: Brand New Day made over $2.5 billion worldwide and Avengers: Doomsday is looking hot, hot, hot!

But even after the uneven Multiverse Saga ends (hopefully on a high note), Marvel Studios won’t be stopping. So, we've put together a list of all the upcoming MCU movies and shows confirmed so far.

While the MCU isn't stopping, Marvel has slowed its roll, with the powers that be returning to the “quality over quantity” approach that defined Marvel Studios’ Infinity Saga output. This means no more than three movies per year and, perhaps more importantly, severely cutting down on TV productions, with a focus on multi-season shows rather than limited series that should’ve been a movie.

It’s a time of change for both Disney and Marvel, but it seems everyone agrees the big screen reigns supreme, so expect a thinner streaming output and more relevant movies starring characters you actually know.

More will be revealed in due time, but for now, here’s what lies at the Multiverse Saga’s end and beyond...

Spoilers ahead for the Marvel Cinematic Universe so far.

Watch Marvel movies and shows on Disney+:Disney+ (With Ads): $11.99/monthDisney+ Premium (No Ads): $18.99/month or $189.99/year

Release date: December 18, 2026 | Director: Anthony & Joe Russo | Cast: Chris Hemsworth, Chris Evans, Pedro Pascal, Robert Downey Jr.

Earth’s Mightiest Heroes (from different Earths, actually) are assembling again in December 2026.

Avengers: Doomsday's cast looks ridiculously stacked, and it’ll finally realize the dream of bringing together the Avengers, the Fantastic Four, and the X-Men (Fox’s original ones, that is) on the big screen. It’s a lot to absorb, and we don’t really know what's going on, but the trailers released so far are promising.

Anthony & Joe Russo (Captain America: The Winter Soldier & Civil War, Avengers: Infinity War & Endgame) are returning to direct, so that’s a good reason to be hyped even if the duo’s post-Marvel career hasn’t been the most exciting. Stephen McFeely (one of their two go-to scribes) is also back, and Michael Waldron (Loki) is helping out as well. It’s an all-star team for the most ambitious MCU project to date, at least until it all culminates in...

Release window: March 2027 | Showrunner: Dario Scardapane | Cast: Charlie Cox, Mike Colter, Finn Jones, Krysten Ritter

Daredevil: Born Again’s debut season was far from perfect, but most viewers agreed that Season 2 was a marked improvement.

Hopefully, that energy will continue in the third and final outing, as the Defenders reunite, with Finn Jones, Krysten Ritter, and Mike Colter all returning from their Netflix shows. Another shocker is the (unofficially) confirmed return of Elodie Yung’s Elektra.

We suspect some of these characters will be transferred to movies post-Secret Wars. In any case, Born Again’s final season should be packed, especially if Marvel Television is sticking to eight or nine episodes.

Release date: December 17, 2027 | Director: Anthony & Joe Russo | Cast: Chris Hemsworth, Chris Evans, Pedro Pascal, Robert Downey Jr.

Practically nothing about the follow-up to Avengers: Doomsday has been revealed yet (though we assume the MCU’s main players will be part of the ensemble), but we know it fully starts shooting in late 2026 and is eyeing a Christmas 2027 arrival. The plan is to leave a year-long wait between the two event movies, leaving fans hanging like back in the MCU’s glory days.

The title comes from Jonathan Hickman’s Secret Wars (2015), which is probably the main source of inspiration for the upcoming big-screen event. Incursions (realities bleeding into each other) have already been set up during the Multiverse Saga, and we know Doomsday directly deals with the multiverse’s breaking point, so it’s easy to see where the larger picture is going.

No spoilers here, but prepare for a very different kind of Avengers flick if Battleworld is indeed the main setting.

Release date: May 5, 2028 | Director: Jake Schreier | Cast: Kit Connor, Sadie Sink, Adam Driver, Christopher Abbott

Whatever happens in Secret Wars (we’ve heard Marvel Studios intends to soft-reboot), Phase Seven of the MCU will kick off with a long-awaited, fresh take on the X-Men — now part of the larger Marvel universe housing all characters. Thunderbolts* director Jake Schreier will be directing, with the same writing team from that movie joining him for another Marvel adventure.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day already did some heavy lifting when it came to setting up one of its leads (Sadie Sink’s Jean Grey), but it’s unclear how the whole group will be assembled.

We know for sure Cyclops (Kit Connor), Rogue (Inde Navarrette), Emma Frost (Samara Weaving), Storm (Maya Boyd), Angel (Asa Germann), Charles Xavier (Christopher Abbott), and Mr. Sinister (Adam Driver) are confirmed to appear, but the cast should grow in the coming months.

Release date: July 28, 2028 | Director: Shawn Levy | Cast: Ryan Gosling (more to be confirmed)

Phase Seven’s second movie will be an unexpected one, but the fan reaction to its reveal was glowing: Ghost Rider, starring Ryan Gosling, with Deadpool & Wolverine’s Shawn Levy directing.

The duo worked together on Star Wars: Starfighter, and it seems it went so well that Disney and Marvel are happy with them reviving the Spirit of Vengeance as the MCU expands its dark borders.

It’s too early to even know which Ghost Rider that Gosling will be playing (Johnny Blaze or Danny Ketch) or where the plot is going, but considering Levy’s past movies, we’re expecting an adventurous tone that blends well with Ghost Rider’s very striking, hellish visuals and darker themes.

Of course, this project is an invitation to add more magical beings to the MCU and explore the Strange-adjacent side of it. Maybe it’s our first step towards a Midnight Sons event movie? We can only hope.

Release date: December 15, 2028 | Director: Ryan Coogler | Cast: David Jonsson, Denzel Washington, Letitia Wright, Winston Duke

Ryan Coogler has taken a break from Marvel to make the excellent Sinners and help create a new iteration of The X-Files, but he’s confirmed to be coming back to wrap up his epic Black Panther trilogy. A while back, he confirmed he’d convinced Denzel Washington to join the MCU, and it sounds like those plans haven’t changed.

We also have a new T’Challa: David Jonsson (Alien: Romulus), who’s meant to play the son of the original T’Challa (Chadwick Boseman). If the years don’t make sense considering he was a kid in Wakanda Forever, wait until Secret Wars’ “soft reboot” for the answers.

What we know for sure is that series veterans Letitia Wright and Winston Duke are expected to stick around, but no plot details are available yet.

Release window: 2028 | Showrunner: Unconfirmed | Cast: Unconfirmed

Revealed at NYCC 2026, Zodiac is set to be Marvel Television’s next ongoing series after Daredevil: Born Again is over. Little is known about the premise at this point, though TV boss Brad Winderbaum has confirmed it’s a “globetrotting, international espionage show about secrets and lies and betrayals” with a packed cast of characters.

Word is the show is, more specifically, a British spy thriller with three leads, two male and one female. It’s expected to shoot in London during spring 2027, and chances are we’ll know much more about it well before that.

Of course, longtime Marvel TV fans are hoping for an Agents of SHIELD revival of sorts (its canonicity was never entirely clear), but it seems this show isn’t exactly that, though Clark Gregg (Agent Coulson) might be involved.

We’ve learned to never say never when it comes to Marvel comebacks, so stay tuned for more news.

Release windows: October 2027 / October 2028 / October 2029 | Showrunner: Bryan Andrews | Cast: Unconfirmed

Following a four-episode season in 2025, the animated series Marvel Zombies will be returning for three consecutive years (starting in 2027) just in time for Halloween.

The twist is that we’re now looking at three two-part specials: The Winter Soldier, The Fist of Khonshu, and The Last Guardian. It’s a huge departure from the previous plans with the Zombies and What If...? series, but it's one that could pay off.

Nothing is known about these small-scale projects at this point, but we know Marvel Zombies was a large enough hit on Disney+ to warrant more, and we’re okay with being surprised when it comes to format.

One has to assume these specials could work as one-shot comic books, but it’ll be interesting to see whether Marvel Television can tell cohesive and compelling stories with even shorter story arcs.

#884. Friedel group completes Shrewsbury Town takeover

Roland Wycherley has been Shrewsbury Town owner and chairman since 1996

Shrewsbury Town's long-drawn-out takeover deal has been completed, allowing former USA international goalkeeper Brad Friedel to come in as the Shropshire outfit's new sporting director.

The paperwork on the share purchase agreement with Scott Davidson's American-based consortium Biscayne ST LLC - which includes Friedel - has been finalised, taking up 87.4 per cent of the League Two club's shares and allowing long-time owner Roland Wycherley to finally let go.

Miami-based businessman Davidson is joined on the new Town board by New York financier Will Dotson and Craig Graham, chairman of Spartans, the Edinburgh-based Scottish League Two club, while former Liverpool, Blackburn Rovers, Aston Villa and Tottenham Hotspur keeper Friedel will come in to take a hands-on role, working with manager Gavin Cowan.

Davidson becomes chairman of the board, which still includes existing members Liam Dooley, the club's chief executive, and Duncan Montgomery, while another ex-goalkeeper, Bryan Finnerty, is to join the group, pending the EFL's owners and directors' tests.

After 30 years of leading the Shropshire club, since succeeding Ray Bailey as chairman in the summer of 1996, Wycherley can now retire at the age of 85.

The Shrewsbury-born lifelong fan first made his intention clear to sell more than five years ago when the Town were still a League One club.

But his dogged determination to do a deal he had to be convinced was right for the club's long-term future before he handed over the reins has made the Shropshire businessman a tough adversary - and lengthened the process, to the frustration of Town fans.

In a club statement,, external Wycherley said his ownership tenure had been "an honour and a privilege" but admitted the club "needed new investment".

Shrewsbury Town takeover completed - looking back at last 30 years

We took our time, says Shrewsbury Town owner Wycherley

After suffering relegation in his first season, Shrewsbury have since been relegated three more times - and promoted three times - in Wycherley's period as owner.

But the biggest legacy of his three decades at the helm was the Town's move in 2007 from their old Gay Meadow home to a new 10,000 all-seater stadium.

The first of those three promotions was under Graham Turner, who returned to the club to recreate the success they had in the late 1970s and early 1980s, taking them up in 2012.

"Roland has put an awful lot into the football club," Turner told BBC Radio Shropshire. "He's kept it going, when at times it's been hard.

"I've nothing but admiration for him. Over the years he's done a very good job."

Wycherley's last game watching the club while at the helm was Saturday's 2-1 FA Cup first-round win at non-league Eastleigh.

Wycherley leaves Town lying 15th in the table, but they are only two points shy of a play-off place and have performed encouragingly this season under manager Gavin Cowan, who came back to the club in January to save them from the drop.

Town were up to eighth when they won at Crawley on 20 October - and have only slipped down in a tightly-congested table thanks to a late Rotherham equaliser followed by a late Gillingham winner a week later.

Friedel was in attendance at Oteley Road for Town's EFL Trophy Northern Group E win over Everton Under-21s on 27 October. And both he and Davidson are expected to be in attendance for this Saturday's home game with another promotion-winning former Town manager Micky Mellon's Oldham Athletic.

Brad Friedel spent the majority of his previous time in English football with Blackburn Rovers, for whom he made 356 of his 653 club appearances

BBC Radio Shropshire sports editor Nick Southall

For years, Shrewsbury Town supporters have awaited certainty over the club's future. Now, they have it.

After 30 years at the helm, Roland Wycherley's reign is over - the Football League's longest-serving owner.

The 85-year-old is credited by many with saving Shrewsbury when an ageing, flood-prone Gay Meadow was becoming an increasing burden on finances.

During his stewardship came some of the most memorable moments in the club's history: the Great Escape at Exeter, Jimmy Quinn's side winning promotion back to the Football League at the first attempt, Graham Turner's fairytale return, another promotion and then a League One Wembley play-off final under Paul Hurst.

Perhaps Wycherley's greatest achievement was overseeing the emotional move from the much-loved Meadow to Oteley Road, securing Town's long-term future.

For many years, the club earned a reputation as one of the best-run in the EFL, operating sustainably, avoiding the financial crises that have engulfed so many others.

Yet football has changed dramatically. Revenues have grown, investor-backed clubs have become increasingly common and Town find it harder to compete financially. While stability remained a strength, supporters increasingly questioned whether the club had reached its limits.

Wycherley's biggest footballing regret may be the missed opportunity to reach the Championship.

Hurst's side came agonisingly close in 2018, only to suffer Wembley heartbreak against Rotherham and miss a return to the second tier for the first time since the 1980s. Likewise, Steve Cotterill's side knocked on the door in 2022-23 but injuries at the tail-end of the season ultimately scuppered his chances.

Many Town supporters have only ever known Wycherley as owner. Now a new chapter begins as Davidson arrives with a track record of success in Scottish football, while Friedel brings both profile and experience from the game's highest levels.

Their arrival raises expectations. Can fresh investment improve recruitment, infrastructure and long-term ambitions? Could Shrewsbury become a success story in the next decade?

"Shrewsbury Town is a special club with a unique place in the landscape - and we believe it has limitless potential.

"We have put together a world-class investment team of business, legal, finance and sports professionals to help guide us and support our growth.

"Paired with the outstanding staff and leadership team that is already in place, our goal is to provide the community and our supporters with a club of which we can all be proud."

"It has been an honour and a privilege to serve as chairman and custodian of my boyhood football club, which I have proudly supported since the age of seven.

"My journey began by sponsoring an advertising board behind the Tech End goalmouth, before becoming an associate director in 1994, vice-chairman and, in 1996, chairman.

"One of the proudest moments was securing the move to our purpose-built stadium in 2007, bringing an end to 97 memorable years at the much-loved Gay Meadow. I firmly believe that move provided the club with a platform to progress.

"The club needs new investment to build on the foundations already in place, particularly the excellent work being undertaken within our foundation and also our academy."

#883. Jamie Lee Curtis Details Close Bond With Rob Reiner's Kids Jake, Romy

Jamie Lee Curtis shared how she’s supporting Rob Reiner and Michele Singer Reiner’s kids Jake Reiner and Romy Reiner nearly a year after their parents’ deaths: “We are family.”

Jamie Lee Curtis is holding Jake Reiner and Romy Reiner close as they continue to navigate their family tragedy.

Nearly one year after Rob Reiner and his wife Michele Singer Reiner were murdered in their Los Angeles home, The Bear alum—a longtime friend of the family—shed light on her bond with the late couple’s kids as they continue to grieve the loss of their parents.

“Of course, I mean, we are family,” Jamie shared in an interview with Extra published Nov. 6 of her bond with Romy, 28, and Jake, 35. “Something like this brings people so much closer.”

“Jake and I were sitting shoulder-to-shoulder doing an interview,” she continued, “and just feeling him there is emotional, and then of course him talking about his parents and their fantastic relationship.”

It’s been over 10 months since Rob and Michele were found dead in their Brentwood, Calif., home on Dec. 14.

In July, the couple’s 32-year-old son Nick Reiner was indicted by a grand jury for their murders, with the grand jury alleging that he intentionally killed his parents by means of lying in wait with “a deadly or dangerous weapon”—in this case a knife.

He has pleaded not guilty on two counts of murder with the special circumstance allegations of multiple murders and murder by means of lying in wait, according to Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan J. Hochman.

And while Rob—who also shared daughter Tracy Reiner, 62, with ex Penny Marshall—and Michele were cremated a week after their tragic deaths, their loved ones have yet to gather in a public setting as they continue to mourn.

“There hasn’t been a big public memorial yet,” Jamie told Extra, “and so we’re all grieving.”

Yet, the Freaky Friday actress has made sure to honor Rob’s legacy on the world’s stage.

In fact, Jamie paid tribute to the late “cherished legend” during the 2026 Emmys In Memoriam segment in September, getting emotional as she highlighted Rob’s achievements, including winning a posthumous Emmy for his work on The Bear.

“He now holds the record of 48 years for the longest gap between acting Emmys, which was previously held by his father Carl Reiner at 37 years,” the Halloween alum shared. "He was generous and kind, and funny as hell, and a friend to all. And we all miss Rob and Michele.”

While looking back at her heartfelt tribute, Jamie—mom to kids Annie and Ruby with husband Christopher Guest—shared insight into her decades-long bond with the family.

“I’m obviously a close friend of theirs; we got married at Rob’s house on Dec. 18, 1984. Rob was the best man,” she recalled to The Hollywood Reporter in an interview published Oct. 23. “My late sister Kelly was my maid of honor. So we are close. Rob is our daughter Annie’s godfather. When Michele married Rob, she and Rob became my daughter’s godparents. We have a closeness, of course.”

As Jamie put it, “What I’m trying to say is that I felt a responsibility to represent everyone—strangers, fans, colleagues, friends, close friends and family—in that moment at the Emmys.”

To see how more stars have paid tribute to the Reiners, keep reading…

The actress, who Rob Reiner adopted during his marriage to late ex Penny Marshall, said she saw her dad at a family gathering the day before he and his wife Michele Singer Reiner were found dead in an apparent homicide at their Los Angeles home.

“I came from the greatest family ever,” she told NBC News in a Dec. 14 statement. “I don’t know what to say. I’m in shock.”

"Oh how we will miss this man," the actress wrote on Instagram. "Thank you, Rob and Michelle, for the way you believe in true love, in fairy tales, and in laughter. Thank you for your faith in the best in people, and for your profound love of our country."Meg continued of her When Harry Met Sally director and Michele, "I have to believe that their story will not end with this impossible tragedy, that some good may come, some awareness raised… I don’t know, but my guess is that they would want that to be hopeful and humane, to be something that brings us all to a greater understanding of one another and to some peace."

“Rob was a friend and collaborator through much of my life," the Spinal Tap actor shared to Instagram. "He was funny, he was smart, he was a mensch. When he came to see the comedy act I was in, and, later, the musical comedy I had co-written, his laugh was uproarious and audible around the block."

Harry recalled that when he, Michael McKean, Christopher Guest and Rob had ideas for films, Rob "was the one who wrote them on 3x5 cards, and organized them into a movie."

"Michele was a very good friend to my wife Judith," he added. "This is unspeakable, the stuff of Greek tragedy."

The Princess Bride star said she's "deeply shocked and devastated" by Rob and Michele's passing.

"It is truly heartbreaking," she shared in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter. "Rob was one of the most loving, compassionate, and kind people I have ever known. He was an extraordinary director and the impact he had on me has stayed with me throughout my career."

"The loss of Rob and Michele is absolutely devastating," the actress wrote on Instagram. "They were not only important to our close community but Rob touched so many millions globally with his art."

She continued of her Alex & Emma director, "Rob was one of the greats. Inspiring so many of us with his ability to craft films that are humorous, powerful, inspirational. He knew no genre, only great storytelling."

The two-time Oscar winner said she saw Rob and Michele one day before they were found dead at their Los Angeles home.

Remembering the late couple as "wonderful, caring, smart, funny, generous people," she wrote on Instagram Dec. 15, "I saw them night before last looking healthy and happy. I am reeling with grief. Stunned."

"They were amazing people and wonderful parents who gave of themselves to make the world a better place," the actress shared on Instagram of her A Few Good Man director and his wife. "My heart, thoughts, and prayers are with their family, friends, and all that are affected by this tragedy."

Demi added Rob and Michele's three children "grew up together" with her and ex Bruce Willis' daughters Rumer Willis, Scout Willis and Tallulah Willis.

"We worked together," she wrote, "and as our lives intertwined personally and professionally I will always cherish the moments and memories of what we shared."

Posting a photo of his and Rob's chairs on the set of The Princess Bride, the actor captioned on Instagram in reaction to the director's passing, "No words."

The Stand By Me alum spoke out about the "HORRIBLE NEWS" of his director and Michele's passing, writing on X, "ALL I CAN SAY IS IM SHOCKED & SADDENED, BUT I #LOVE U ROB! U WILL B 4EVER MISSED!"

"One of my most cherished pictures," the A Simple Favor director captioned on X. "Rob was my true hero. A true visionary titan and a lovely lovely person."

He continued, "One never knows if it’s proper to post during something as tragic as this. But I just want the world to know what so many of us know in the industry. Rob was the best."

The actress was "absolutely devastated" as she paid tribute to Rob, who played her father on New Girl.

"My heart is broken," she wrote on Instagram. "Rob Reiner was the absolute warmest, funniest, most generous of spirits. A truly good human being. An incredible artist and such a playful and fun collaborator. I cherish the time we spent working together and the many films he made that have shaped who I am."

She added, "Rob and his lovely wife Michele were always so kind and it brought me so much joy any time I was lucky enough to see them."

The Stand By Me actor learned of his director's death through costar Jerry O'Connell, writing on his website Dec. 15 that he was "still processing and coming to grips with a tragic, senseless, devastating loss."

Wil went on to recount how Rob made him "feel loved, valued, seen, and respected" amid his own strained relationship with his parents during the making of the1986 movie.

"Rob was a good person who put great art into the world, who made a positive difference in more lives than any of us can imagine," he added. "The world is a better place thanks to his activism and the way he chose to use all of his privilege and influence."

"My husband Brad and I had the great honor and pleasure of working with Rob and Michele Reiner often and happily in movies and television where their impact as actor, director, and producer will be everlasting," the Seinfeld alum wrote on Instagram. "Even more deeply felt was their superb example of how to be an activist and a powerful voice for the environment, for justice, and for democracy. They were great American patriots, and they were so much fun. We send our condolences and love to the Reiner family."

The Abbott Elementary star recalled how her "first ever television role was a scene" with Rob, writing on Instagram Story, "I was proud to work with and get to talk about comedy with him over time."

"I'm speechless," she continued. "What a tragic loss."

"Michelle and I are heartbroken by the tragic passing of Rob Reiner and his beloved wife, Michele," the former president wrote on X. "Rob’s achievements in film and television gave us some of our most cherished stories on screen. But beneath all of the stories he produced was a deep belief in the goodness of people—and a lifelong commitment to putting that belief into action."

He continued, "Together, he and his wife lived lives defined by purpose. They will be remembered for the values they championed and the countless people they inspired. We send our deepest condolences to all who loved them."

The actor, who was directed by Rob in 1986's Stand By Me, shared a photo of himself on set with the director on Instagram, simply saying, "Love you, Rob. Sincerely."

"I don't mean this as any offense to my parents—Rob was like a father to me," he added on CBS Mornings Dec. 15. "He was like a father to me. It's just surreal."

Jerry continued, "Everything I have is because of Rob Reiner. Everything I have. It's just a shocking day."

The family of the late television icon released an emotional statement noting how close the duo were.

"The Lear Family is devastated by the deaths of Rob and Michele Reiner," they told Deadline. "Norman often referred to Rob as a son, and their close relationship was extraordinary, to us and the world."

"Norman would have wanted to remind us that Rob and Michele spent every breath trying to make this country a better place," the statement continued, "and they pursued that through their art, their activism, their philanthropy, and their love for family and friends. Lyn Lear had remained very close with them and said, 'The world is unmistakably darker tonight, and we are left bereft.'"

"Christopher and I are numb and sad and shocked about the violent, tragic deaths of our dear friends Rob and Michelle Singer Reiner," Jamie Lee said in a statement to Variety, "and our ONLY focus and care right now is for their children and immediate families and we will offer all support possible to help them."

The couple added, "There will be plenty of time later to discuss the creative lives we shared and the great political and social impact they both had on the entertainment industry, early childhood development, the fight for gay marriage and their global care for a world in crisis. We have lost great friends. Please give us time to grieve."

After news of Rob and Michele's passing broke, the Magic of Belle Isle star wrote on Instagram of her director and his wife, "God be with those who love them. Thank you Rob for giving us so much joy to hold on to."

"The humor is smart and the heart is real," the actor, who costarred with Rob's dad Carl Reiner in 2003's Good Boy!, shared on X. "His films were part of the air for us. Grateful for what he made, and for what he and his wife gave the world.

The Monty Python alum tweeted that he had spoken to Rob on the phone the night before his death.

"Rob Reiner was a lovely man. I spoke to him last night for over an hour," he wrote on X. "I always enjoyed his company. I met him at his Dad's in 1975. He was telling me about fiming at Stonehenge and his thoughts for the future. This is so awful. I shall miss him. A clever, talented and very thoughtful man. So awful."

The Misery star said she was "absolutely devasted" by the news of Rob's death.

"I loved Rob," Kathy, who worked with the director in the 1990 film, told NBC in a statement. "He was brilliant and kind, a man who made films of every genre to challenge himself as an artist."

She continued, "He changed the course of my life. Michele was a gifted photographer. She shot my beautiful photos for the Misery campaign. My heart breaks for them both. My thoughts are with their family."

"Shocked by the death of Rob Reiner," the actor shared on X, 40 years after working with the director in 1985's The Sure Thing. "A great man."

The actor, who worked with the director in the 1994 movie North, wrote on X, "Horrified to hear of the passing of Rob Reiner and his wonderful wife Michelle [sic]. So much love to their kids and family."

"Rob Reiner was an almost indescribably wonderful man," she wrote on X. "Kind, jovial, thoughtful, and generous. He shaped our industry of course, and more so the world around us, making films that centered empathy and humor. He made us more bold, willing to take risks for love. He used his massive audience and knowledge of how to tell stories to defend democracy, and stand for his neighbors, both near and far."

"And even when the cameras were off, he showed up," Sophia went on. "He was often first to say yes to the organizing work, showing up on zoom after zoom, in support of organizations making the world a better place. He offered his talents and gifts. He said YES in service of others. In the years I’ve been lucky enough to know him in those dedicated spaces, he has influenced and inspired me, for good. I am utterly heartbroken at his and Michele’s deaths, and I am holding his loved ones in my heart today."

"Rob Reiner was one of my favorite directors," the Zoolander alum shared on X. "He made some of the most formative movies for my generation. He came out form behind a huge comedic shadow of the great Carl Reiner and being a tv actor to being a a great director who made an incredible run of movies."

He continued, "Spinal Tap is one of the best comedies ever made—and the list goes on. He was a kind caring person who was really really funny."

"This man's work changed my life and I don't think that's hyperbolic," the Bear actress wrote on her Instagram Stories. "I was so fortunate to have met him recently and couldn't believe how game he was to talk to me—and now just because he wanted to indulge a young fan."

She continued, "But because he really loved what he did and the friends he got to do it with. He was so generous with his time and energy and stories. Feeling absolutely gutted."

"I’m absolutely shocked and horrified to hear about Rob Reiner and his wife Michele," the comedian wrote on X. "This is a travesty. Praying for swift justice. Sympathies to their family and children. I’m at a loss for words."

"Grieving the loss of my favorite director of all-time," the Emmy winner shared on Instagram. "A Few Good Men is THE reason I became an actor, and Rob’s filmography behind the camera is THE reason I wanted to direct and still do."

He added, "I hate that Rob and his wife are gone from this world, but they sure as hell impacted me and countless others while here."

In the wake of Rob and Michele's death, the musician recalled meeting the couple while working on the yet-to-be released Spinal Tap at Stonehenge: The Final Finale.

"He and Michele made me feel like family and gave me an incredible opportunity to fulfill a dream," Josh shared on Instagram. "There was laughter and love and song and it was a memory I will cherish forever. I'm stunned and deeply saddened and sending my love to their family.

#881. 'Tinkerman' Alonso's Chelsea side still searching for identity

Struggling Sunderland get a narrow win at home against Chelsea

Constant changes in formation and personnel - and another disappointing defeat.

Xabi Alonso's frustration was obvious as Chelsea's struggles for identity continued in the 1-0 defeat by Sunderland.

It is starting to feel as though the Spaniard is the latest "Tinkerman" at Stamford Bridge, a moniker first associated with Blues boss Claudio Ranieri back in 2002-03.

For the first time this season, Chelsea lined up with a three-man midfield - but they were also without a recognised striker for the second match in a row, with Pedro Neto again struggling to lead the line in their loss at the Stadium of Light.

By contrast, struggling Sunderland were led by target man Brian Brobbey, who won a 36th-minute penalty after being brought down by Levi Colwill. Enzo le Fee converted the game's only goal from the spot.

That decision came moments after Chelsea were denied a penalty when Cole Palmer went down under a challenge from Luke O'Nien, but the video assistant referee ruled that contact had started outside the box.

Those two incidents in quick succession meant Alonso and his coaching staff appeared angry on the touchline after the Sunderland goal.

However, the Chelsea manager refused to criticise the officials after the game - instead he gave brief answers that changed the subject and were critical towards his players for not carrying out the gameplan properly.

Asked whether Brobbey was simply unstoppable, Alonso, 44, replied: "No, he's stoppable. He's stoppable, but we have to do it better than we did today.

"Out of almost nothing he got a couple of chances. He got the penalty as well.

"I'm not happy with how we defended that situation. It's something that we could have avoided, something that we had worked on during the week. To concede penalties is not good for us."

It left nowhere to hide for Colwill, who was substituted at half-time, with Moises Caicedo filling in at centre-back despite having barely completed a full training session all week and needing careful management of his own fitness issues.

Chelsea also created few clear chances, aside from a headed opportunity that Â£117m signing Morgan Rogers squandered, while Palmer also struggled - days after being left out of the England squad.

Before the season started, Alonso said he wanted his Chelsea side to be "unpredictable".

Although factors such as injuries are beyond his control, his side have achieved that, but to their own detriment.

Failed to deal with Brobbey - player ratings for Sunderland v Chelsea

Sunderland beat Chelsea for first league win since August

Chelsea have five wins, four losses and a draw in 10 Premier League games under Xabi Alonso

Only Tottenham (28) have made more more line-up changes than Chelsea (24) in the Premier League this season.

In the early part of the campaign, they at least had a settled and exciting front three of Joao Pedro, Rogers and Palmer.

It was largely the reason behind the positive start to the season despite failing to keep a clean sheet against top-flight opposition until Alonso's eighth game in charge.

With Caicedo injured, they suffered problems in midfield and continued to make changes from match to match, while also experimenting with personnel to fix the defence.

However, they largely looked on course to emulate the back-three system Alonso excelled with during his historic German double-winning season at Bayer Leverkusen in 2023-24.

As Caicedo returned after the international break, however, captain Reece James was injured.

Joao Pedro featured in wins against Bournemouth and Everton before sustaining a thigh injury, having already missed Brazil's international matches.

Number one goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez broke his jaw in a collision at Everton, while Maxence Lacroix, who had been a near ever-present since joining from Crystal Palace in the summer, is expected to be out until January with a hamstring injury.

Defender Jorrel Hato has also suffered a setback in recent weeks.

It has left Alonso reacting to events when selecting his starting XI, with the Spaniard saying: "There are situations. Yesterday Josh [Acheampong] said he was not ready to play, so we are short of options and we need to walk through this step.

"Even when we win, when we lose, we miss some players that we have injured and for sure we are waiting for them to come back because they are important."

He admitted his side were missing Joao Pedro, although supporters have also been frustrated that Estevao Willian, who came on at half-time on Sunday, has started only one league match this season.

Prior to Sunday's game, Chelsea were averaging just 46% possession. They then dominated the ball at Sunderland (with 68.7% possession) but without creating many significant chances.

Meanwhile, only Crystal Palace have conceded more shots on target than Chelsea's 50, while the Blues top the league with 53 shots on target - meaning there have been plenty of chances at both ends during their matches.

Alonso can still be pleased with Chelsea having collected five more points than they managed from the equivalent fixtures last season, with the club on course to qualify for the Champions League while sitting fifth in the table.

However, that is a low bar after a dismal campaign last season, when Chelsea finished 10th.

Going into the November international break, Alonso remains a long way from establishing a style of play, or an identity capable of bringing consistency - although he promised promising in an interview last week that Chelsea would be "different" and "better" by the end of the season.

"The nation that leads in space will shape the future of humanity."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

President Trump issued a declaration yesterday (Nov. 3), proclaiming space open to all humanity for exploration, and the right of American citizens to develop and settle the solar system according to United States laws.

"The American Declaration of Freedom in Space," describes space as the "province of all humans" and asserts that the United States will lead humanity's expansion into the cosmos. The proclamation reiterates the administration's goals with NASA's Artemis program to return American astronauts to the moon by 2028 and eventually sending astronauts to Mars, but introduces no new funding, programs or policy directives.

"Our Nation will lead the way in the exploration, development, use, and settlement of these new frontiers — forging an interplanetary civilization founded on the enduring and inalienable rights of freedom and individual liberty," the document says.

Trump invoked America's "frontier spirit," highlighting Apollo 11 astronauts as the first people in history to walk on the moon's surface and robotic rovers exploring Mars as examples of U.S. leadership, and emphasized the country's flourishing commercial space sector helping ensure "American space superiority for all eternity."

"The nation that leads in space will shape the future of humanity," the declaration says, and pledges that America will carry the values of faith, freedom and individual liberty into an interplanetary civilization.

The proclamation also highlights the success of NASA's Artemis II mission in April, which carried four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon and set a record for the farthest humans have ever traveled from Earth. The follow-up to that mission, Artemis III, is scheduled to launch next summer (2027), and will test rendezvous and docking operations between NASA's Orion spacecraft and the program's two commercial lunar landers in low Earth orbit.

Artemis IV will be the program's first lunar landing mission, and is targeted for 2028. A December 2025 executive order from the President reaffirmed the goal of meeting that timeline, as well as the deployment of the initial elements for a permanent lunar outpost by 2030.

Trump's declaration yesterday does not establish new NASA programs, allocate additional funding or issue instructions to federal agencies. Its sweeping language, though, does echo some of the principles in the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which guarantees freedom of exploration while prohibiting national sovereignty claims on other planets.

Josh Dinner is Space.com's Spaceflight Staff Writer and a photographer with a passion for science and exploration. He has worked the space beat since 2016, covering the evolution of NASA's commercial spaceflight partnerships and crewed missions, planetary science missions, the Artemis program and humanity's return to the moon. He also enjoys building 1:144-scale model rockets and spacecraft. Find some of Josh's launch photography on Instagram, and follow him on X, where he mostly posts in haiku.

#876. Palace consider replacing Sage, with Frank among contenders

Liverpool dispatch Palace to pile pressure on Sage

Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage is in serious danger of losing his job only five months into his reign, with the club bottom of the Premier League going into the international break.

Sunday's 3-1 defeat by Liverpool was Palace's fourth successive league loss, with Sage's side having won just two of their 10 league matches this season.

The club have held internal talks aimed at deciding Sage's future and his potential successor.

Former Tottenham and Brentford manager Thomas Frank is viewed as a strong candidate, while ex-Nottingham Forest boss Sean Dyche also has some support internally.

Both are out of work and would be available to start immediately.

Palace have taken just seven points from their 10 league matches and have the worst defensive record in the league, having conceded 24 goals.

They are also 21st in the Europa League, currently enough for a play-off spot, with only one win from their four matches.

If he is dismissed, Frenchman Sage could become the first managerial casualty of the Premier League season.

He was appointed on a three-year contract in June after Oliver Glasner departed at the end of last season.

"It's not from the dream to the nightmare," the 47-year-old said after the defeat by Liverpool.

"I'm not feeling this. I'm just in my job, and focusing on my job, and what I have to do to find the solution.

"The results are not at this level, and I know I have to push more on those things, especially in our way of playing, to make that move."

Sage previously led Lens to a second-place finish in Ligue 1 and a first French Cup triumph in their 120-year history.

However, he has been unable to replicate Glasner's success at Palace. Glasner, who now manages Nottingham Forest, led Palace to a first FA Cup title and a Europa Conference League triumph.

Palace are winless in the league since 11 October, with their losing run sparked by a 5-0 loss to fierce rivals Brighton.

After that match, Sage said he felt "shame" and admitted he did not know if he would be given time to turn Palace's fortunes around.

However, there was a degree of sympathy from some behind the scenes.

Injuries were not kind to his plans, while the absence of Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaila Sarr - due to a mixture of fitness and personal issues, related to both players' desire to leave the club - did not help the start of his reign.

However, three more league defeats have followed, with Palace hitting the bar and having a goal ruled out in their loss to Liverpool at Selhurst Park.

"We have to be more competitive," Sage said on Sunday.

"At the moment, we create some things, we expect a lot of things, but we don't have the results expected."

Palace's next Premier League match is at Coventry on 21 November following the two-week international break.

#874. Scottish roundup: flying Falkirk hit five to shatter Hearts’ long unbeaten home run

Falkirk leapfrog their hosts with 5-2 rout at Tynecastle

Liam Scales gives Celtic 1-0 home win over Kilmarnock

Falkirk obliterated Hearts’ 18-month unbeaten home record in the Scottish Premiership with a stunning 5-2 win at Tynecastle on Sunday as they leapfrogged their hosts into third place.

Wouter Vrancken’s beleaguered side, missing 11 players through injury, were in disarray as Falkirk romped into a five-goal lead early in the second half through Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double. Hearts hit back through Sabri Guendouz, on as a substitute, and a Cláudio Braga penalty, but Falkirk were well worthy of making it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1995.

Vrancken said: “This is an embarrassment, the first half for sure. It’s crazy, crazy, and everybody – me, staff, players – have to take responsibility in those things. This is ridiculous.”

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle for Hearts since April 2025 and they have won just two of their past 11 matches. Falkirk move into third, a point above Hearts, although they have played a game more.

Liam Scales provided a looping finish to secure a 1-0 home victory for Celtic against Kilmarnock later on Sunday. The Irish defender hooked a Camilo Durán cross into the top corner in the 26th minute to restore Celtic’s four-point lead at the top of the table.

Celtic – and Kasper Høgh in particular – otherwise had a frustrating day in front of goal, with Benjamin Nygren missing a second-half penalty. Høgh had an early goal disallowed as his barren run without scoring hit 16 games since a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on his second appearance.

The Celtic manager, Martin O’Neill, said: “I thought Kasper was off the mark for about 35 seconds. I think he would maybe have scored the next chance if the first had counted, but he worked really hard for us.”

Rangers banished their recent away day blues with a solid 2-0 win at St Mirren on Saturday.

Draws against Dundee and Hearts in their past two Scottish Premiership games away from Ibrox had blemished their title challenge, but Derek McInnes’s side were determined to leave Paisley without a mark on them.

The in-form striker Ryan Naderi scored with a soft penalty after 18 minutes before the returning captain, Dan Neil, added a second just after the hour with a deflected strike to extend Rangers’ unbeaten run in all competitions to 12 games.

The Aberdeen manager, Stephen Robinson, insists he will face the challenge head on as his side go into the international break in real trouble at the wrong end of the table.

Hibernian started the evening three points behind Robinson’s side, but a dominant second-half performance in a 4-0 victory at Pittodrie allowed the Edinburgh club to overtake their hosts in 10th place on goal difference.

The hosts showed promise early in the game and the Hibs keeper Raphael Sallinger saved well from Jack Milne, who also hit the bar for Aberdeen before Jamie McGrath’s 25-yard strike found the target. Aberdeen went all-out in search of an equaliser, but quickly fell 2-0 behind to Callum Wright, sparking calls for Robinson’s head from the home support. Further strikes from Thibault Klidjé and Nicky Cadden completed the rout.

Robinson said: “It’s really, really disappointing, there’s no hiding away from it. It was an unacceptable performance and an unacceptable result. We haven’t taken our chances – Hibs had five or six chances and took four of them – [and] that’s always the difference in football. We got the result we deserved.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

“It’s a difficult situation, difficult for myself, the players and the club. I will keep fighting until told otherwise. We have to be better than that, that’s not acceptable. We have to get players who want to fight and try to get us out of this situation.”

Jim Goodwin, the home manager, hit out at the decision to award the penalty that cost Dundee United dear in a 1-1 draw against Motherwell at Tannadice.

The referee, Ryan Lee, had initially given a free-kick for offside in the early stages of the game. However, he was then advised by the VAR, Andrew Dallas, to have another look at an incident where Tawanda Maswanhise had gone down in the United box under a challenge by the home captain, Dylan Tait. After checking the pitchside monitor, the referee pointed to the spot with the Motherwell captain, Lukas Fadinger, tucking the penalty away.

The hosts ultimately salvaged a point thanks to Jesse Randall’s goal but Goodwin insisted his side should have had all three. “It’s a poor decision for me,” he said. “I know it’s going to be subjective and people will have their own opinions on it, but I don’t know what Dylan Tait is meant to do.”

Unsurprisingly, the Motherwell manager, Alfred Johansson, disagreed with Goodwin’s assessment, saying: “He’s on the ball and gets down from a tackle, and it’s a penalty.”

Simo Valakari was thrilled to give St Johnstone supporters a 2-1 victory against Dundee to celebrate after recent Perth struggles against their Tayside rivals.

Josh Campbell headed the home side in front after five minutes. Joe Westley, on as a substitute, replied early in the second half after a mix-up between the keeper Ross Sinclair and Cheick Diabate. Kai Fotheringham, on his first Premiership start for St Johnstone, scored a deflected winner on 72 minutes.

Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan.

For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket. The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff.

Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause? Likely a problem with the first stage motor.

The mission lost 13 tiny satellites known as cubesats. Cubesats are a popular option for space missions, because they are small and cheap, and they often operate in swarms. After failing to launch this batch of cubesats, the Super Strypi program never recovered from its failure, and the Air Force never tried launching another one.

The Super Strypi rocket was a 21st century take on a 1960s rocket. It was designed to be a modern version of the three-stage Strypi sounding rocket used for for reentry vehicle and anti-missile target tests. Its three stages, powered by Aerojet Rocketdyne solid rocket motors, was designed to reach orbit, rather than suborbital trajectories common to most sounding rockets.

The U.S. Air Force hoped Super Strypi would be a new tool for quick-response launches based on national security needs. Altogether, it was designed to launch small payloads of up to 300 kilograms into space for a mere $15 million per mission.

The rocket's primary payload was the ORS-4 satellite, short for Operationally Responsive Space 4, which was built for the Air Force by engineers at the University of Hawaii (who nicknamed it HiakaSat). It was designed to capture Earth imagery and monitor the environment over the course of a year.

The 12 other payloads on Super Strypi included eight cubesats for NASA's Edison Demonstration of Smallsat Networks mission, and as well as four others for universities that had been added as secondary payloads.

Since the Super Strypi failure, neither the Air Force or Space Force has opted to use the rocket for a new mission. The Space Force has turned instead to commercial companies for fast-turnaround launch support.

In June of this year, the U.S. Space Force teamed up with Rocket Lab to launch the Victus Haze mission with just 17 hours of notice, a new record to demonstrate short-turnaround launch response.

As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.

#872. Fan injured after falling through hole in stand

Tromso's Romssa Arena, pictured before a Conference League game against Brighton in August, is 200 miles inside the Arctic Circle

A fan was taken to hospital after a number of Bodo/Glimt supporters fell through a hole in the away stand at Tromso.

The Norwegian top-flight match at Romssa Arena on Sunday was paused just before half-time after Bodo keeper Nikita Haikin called for the referee's attention.

Bodo/Glimt press officer Simen Pedersen told the Reuters news agency that "up to five people fell through the stands".

"We stood and bounced to a supporter song, then the floor gave way," Bodo supporter Andrine Moen told local newspaper Verdens Gang, as reported by Reuters.

"It cracked in two in the row in front of us. There were at least two people who fell through the floor, but we don't know how far they fell or how many fell in total."

The remaining Bodo supporters were moved into other parts of the ground before the match resumed.

The match at Tromso's stadium - the northernmost venue in Norway's Eliteserien - was played in heavy rain.

The score was 0-0 at the time of the incident, but Bodo forward Ola Brynhildsen scored twice after the game resumed to give the league leaders a 2-0 win.

Bodo are locked in a title battle with Viking and the Eliteserien season is set to finish in the first week of December.

#870. FA Cup roundup: Seventh-tier Wimborne shock Crawley to reach second round

Grimsby and Stockport survive scares but Wednesday out

Exeter upset League One leaders Huddersfield

Seventh-tier Wimborne heaped more misery on Crawley as the bottom side in the Football League lost 2-0 in the biggest upset of the FA Cup first round.

The Dorset part-timers took the lead after only nine minutes when the property surveyor Yang Seung-woo curled a superb strike from just inside the penalty area into the top corner.

Crawley came close to equalising when Kai Jennings flashed a low shot narrowly wide before Jonny Russell headed tamely into the arms of the home goalkeeper Cam Plain.

Crawley’s interim manager, Kevin Blackwell, made a triple change at half-time and Charlie Barker fired inches wide for the team 57 places above their hosts in the pyramid. The Southern Premier League South side got a huge slice of luck to seal victory 11 minutes from time. Jackson King’s shot hit Cameron Munn to send the ball squirming beyond the former Arsenal goalkeeper Vito Mannone.

Will Sutton scored a dramatic extra-time winner for Oldham as Dave Challinor’s first game in charge of Sheffield Wednesday ended in an upset. The homegrown central defender was up for a free-kick which the Owls failed to clear, with Sutton left completely free to nod home from six yards and secure a 2-1 win.

Calum Kavanagh put Oldham ahead in the 66th minute with a fierce drive after Mike Fondop headed on Noah Chilvers’ right-wing cross. Wednesday equalised 10 minutes later through the former Oldham forward Davis Keillor-Dunn.

The match ignited further in the 84th minute following a touchline fracas involving a large number of players. The Oldham manager, Micky Mellon, was sent off and Sheffield Wednesday’s Callum Slattery was booked. After Sutton’s winning goal, Oldham defended resolutely to close out the game.

Stafford Rangers were denied a historic win after losing 3-2 on penalties to Grimsby after they drew 3-3 after extra time. Two goals from firefighter Darrhyl Mason and one from the Aston Villa youth coach Jack Birch got the eighth-tier side – 89 places below League Two Grimsby – to a shootout.

Mason and Birch had put Rangers 2-0 ahead in front of a crowd of 3,130 at the Stan Robinson Stadium as they chased the second round for the first time since 2007. But set-piece headers inside three minutes from Harvey Rodgers and Maldini Kacurri sent the tie into extra time, where Mason and Géza Turi traded goals.

The home debutant Luca Navarro had to score to send the tie into sudden death but saw his spot-kick saved by Harvey Cartwright to end Rangers’ nine-match Cup marathon.

Lewis Fiorini’s extra-time penalty sent Stockport, who are second in League One, into the second round after they came from two goals down with 10 men to win 3-2 against Cray Wanderers.

Despite being 112 places below their opponents in the pyramid, it was the Isthmian Premier side Cray who took the lead after 21 minutes when Sammie MacLeod found the bottom corner.

Stockport were then reduced to 10 men in the 31st minute as goalkeeper Luca Ashby-Hammond was sent off for a dangerous challenge on John Ufuah. Alex Hernández bent a brilliant strike into the top corner from the resulting free-kick.

Depleted Stockport pulled one back in the 81st minute when Kyle Wootton tscored with a header. And the Hatters then sent the tie into extra time when Mikael Mandron was in the right place to nod home Jack Diamond’s cross. The decisive moment came in the 101st minute when Cray goalkeeper JJ Briggs clattered into Mandron to give away a penalty, which was dispatched by Fiorini.

Charlie Savage scored against his father’s team as Reading eased into the second round with a 5-0 rout of Peterborough at the Weston Homes Stadium on Saturday.

This all-League One tie turned out to be one of the most one-sided of the day, with the Peterborough manager, Robbie Savage, watching on in disbelief as his side were pulled apart.

Reading went ahead after 26 minutes as slick passing led to Andy Rinomhota playing in Daniel Kyerewaa, who found the bottom corner via a deflection. Reading doubled their lead in the 34th minute when a cross from Haydon Roberts was met by a diving header from top scorer Jack Marriott.

It was in effect game over in first-half stoppage time as Savage deepened his father’s misery when he took possession after the ball ran off Marriott, his deflected effort finding the top corner.

Jamie Reid added a fourth for the visitors in the 72nd minute when Paudie O’Connor nodded Savage’s free-kick into his path for him to lift over the Peterborough goalkeeper Alex Bass. Reading struck yet again four minutes later when Liam Fraser’s pass put Reid clean through to score his second.

Non-league Kidderminster breezed into the second round with a convincing 3-0 victory over League One Doncaster.

The National League club opened the scoring after 22 minutes when Maz Kouhyar pulled the ball back to Lewis Walker, and he fired home at the second attempt after his initial shot had hit the upright.

The Harriers striker continued to cause problems, putting an effort over the bar and another just wide, but in the 36th minute he turned provider, charging upfield before teeing up Kouhyar and the on-loan Notts County midfielder slotted home. Kouhyar was again involved in the third goal, having a shot that Josh Clarke could only parry and David Davis turned in the rebound.

The Kidderminster manager, Paul Wotton, said: “We started well, scored the goal and got the crowd up. It was just a really good day. They are a League One team at the end of the day, no matter what the scoreline suggests. They are two leagues higher than us, so they are going to have moments in the game, but we stood up to it.”

League Two Exeter pulled off an upset with a 2-1 win away to League One leaders Huddersfield. Exeter took the lead after 12 minutes, thanks to a perfectly delivered cross from the left from Luca Woodhouse, with centre-back Jack Taylor stealing in at the far post to finish it off.

Huddersfield looked a different team in the second half and found an equaliser within eight minutes of the restart as Ibane Bowat headed home Cameron Humphreys’ corner at the back post.

Charlie Cummins grabbed the winner nine minutes from time at the end of a well-worked move up the right, culminating in Reece Cole’s cutback and a good finish.

Altrincham were denied another famous FA Cup upset as they conceded an 84-minute equaliser against Notts County before bowing out in a penalty shootout.

County took the lead through Jacob Bedeau in the 28th minute but Altrincham responded well with Lucas Weaver grabbing an equaliser six minutes before half-time. Lewis Banks gave the hosts the lead just before the hour but Callum Roberts dashed Altrincham’s hopes of another cup scalp, having beaten 17 Football League sides in the competition, scoring with a first-time strike to force extra-time.

With neither side able to make a breakthrough in extra-time the game went to penalties and Aidan Barlow, Sam Taylor and Eddy Jones all missed from the spot for Altrincham as County triumphed 3-2.

Blackpool survived a scare at Hornchurch, needing to rely on a 118th-minute winner from Josh Bowler to secure a 2-1 comeback victory at the Hornchurch Stadium.

Fleetwood’s hopes of following up their memorable Carabao Cup upset against Premier League champions Arsenal with a long FA Cup run are over after a 2-1 home defeat by fellow League Two side Rochdale. Baba Adeeko’s goal in extra time at Highbury sent the visitors through.

Chesterfield withstood a second-half comeback from Yeovil Town to secure their place in the second round with a 4-3 victory. Yeovil recovered from 3-1 down to level at 3-3 before Joel Randall struck the winner for the Spireites a minute from time.

Late Mansfield goals from Rhys Oates and Jordan Bowery ended the plucky Cup resistance of National League North Macclesfield. Nathan Moriah-Welsh gave Mansfield a first-half lead but the Silkmen were still in the tie under Oates made it 2-0 in the 72nd minute. Bowery added a third three minutes into added time to wrap up victory for the Stags.

League One Plymouth eased through thanks to three goals in a late 11-minute spell in a 4-0 win against Southern League Premier Central battlers Alvechurch. Will Evans finally broke the deadlock after 50 minutes, winning the ball from Jessy Bavanganga before driving a low angled shot into the far corner. Further goals from Evans, Michael Baidoo and Ronan Curtis saw the Pilgrims through.

League One strugglers Barnsley booked their spot in the second round with a 7-2 win over Aldershot at Oakwell, with Cameron McGeehan grabbing a hat-trick.

Leyton Orient held off Harborough 5-1 to progress into the second round while League Two high-flyers Crewe beat Wimbledon 2-1.

Nick Powell and Adam Phillips scored twice as Bradford thrashed National League North side Marine 7-0, while a late goal from Joel Randall helped Cheltenham close out a dramatic 4-3 win over National League Yeovil.

Last season’s quarter-finalists Port Vale booked their place in the second round with a 4-2 victory over National League strugglers Scunthorpe United at Vale Park. MK Dons avoided an upset as they ground out a 2-1 win over League Two Swindon.

Southern League Premier Central team Worcester’s hopes of an upset were ended in a 1-0 defeat at League Two Colchester while Jack Bates scored twice in the first half as Dover progressed with a 2-0 win over Wealdstone.

Ollie Pearce scored after 10 seconds as York sealed a 4-0 win over Northampton. The City captain also scored a second before Alex Hunt and Josh Stones completed the rout.

Jordan Thewlis’s stoppage-time penalty gave seventh-tier Guiseley a 1-0 win over Sutton at Nethermoor Park as Carlisle beat League Two leaders Salford 1-0. Ryan Graydon missed a penalty for the visitors before David Ajiboye’s goal just before the break proved enough to send the Cumbrians through.

Eighth-tier AFC Rushden & Diamonds slipped to a 4-0 defeat at Burton. Will Collar and Borges Rodrigues scored for the Brewers in the first half, with Charlie Webster and Zac Scutt adding two more late on.

Nathan Odokonyero scored twice as National League South Salisbury saw off seventh-tier Sholing 6-0 to take their place in round two for the first time since reforming in 2015.

#869. Gisele Bündchen Honors "Great Man" Joaquim Valente in Birthday Tribute

Gisele Bündchen gave her husband Joaquim Valente a sweet shoutout for his 39th birthday: “How lucky I am. I love you so much!”

Gisele Bündchen’s husband Joaquim Valente has strutted his way into her heart—and he’s there to stay.

The supermodel gave the jiu-jitsu instructor some love in honor of his 39th birthday, sharing just how grateful she is to have him in her life.

“Today a great man was born, @joaquimvalente,” Bündchen wrote over a photo of the pair on Instagram Stories Nov. 7 in a message translated from Portuguese. “How lucky I am. I love you so much!”

In the sweet snap, Bündchen—wearing a mustard yellow halter top—cozied up to her husband as they both gave the camera a smile.

But this wouldn’t be the first time Bündchen and Valente—who tied the knot in December 2025—have proved they’re a model match.

After all, the Victoria’s Secret Angel—mom to a 19-month-old son with Valente as well as kids Benjamin, 16, and Vivian, 13, with ex-husband Tom Brady—received support from her partner as he stepped out with her for a rare public appearance at the Lotus House’s annual gala, where Bündchen was honored, in Miami, Fla., Oct. 29.

“I feel so grateful to be part of the Lotus House family and to witness all the love and care that [goes] into changing so many lives,” Bündchen wrote on Instagram following the outing. “I’m so honored to be part of this journey alongside the incredible @lotushouseshelter team, all the volunteers, and everyone who gives their time, love, and support in whatever way they can.”

In addition to sharing pics alongside fellow award honoree Karlie Kloss, the 45-year-old—dressed in a button-down shirt, denim jeans and a sun hat—also posted a group photo with Valente.

And it’s clear that the athlete—donning blue jeans, a gray button-down shirt and a brown vest—couldn’t have been happier to be his wife’s cheerleader as he leaned in close to Bündchen while giving the camera a bright smile.

But he doesn’t just show up for Bündchen when it counts. As the Lessons author emphasized on Father’s Day this past June, he also shows up as the best dad.

“Thank you for leading by example, and for the values you embody, love, humility, integrity, discipline, kindness and consistency,” Bündchen wrote in a June 21 Instagram carousel. “You are an incredible role model. We are all so grateful for you, and we love you so much.”

Two spacewalking astronauts will finish upgrading the International Space Station's power system today (Nov. 5), and you can watch the action live.

NASA astronaut Anil Menon and the Canadian Space Agency's Joshua Kutryk will install the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) today, during a roughly seven-hour spacewalk that's scheduled to begin at 8:30 a.m. EST (1330 GMT).

You can watch it live here at Space.com, courtesy of NASA, beginning at 7 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT).

Today's extravehicular activity (EVA) will be the second in a week for Menon and Kutryk, who installed the station's seventh iROSA during an Oct. 29 spacewalk. That excursion was the 100th U.S. spacewalk from the ISS to date, and the first EVA for a Canadian astronaut since 2019.

Today's spacewalk will wrap up an ambitious ISS power upgrade that has taken more than five years to pull off.

"The installation job will complete the years-long process that began in June 2021 to augment the space station’s power generating capacity from 160 kilowatts to about 215 kilowatts," NASA officials wrote about the EVA in a blog post on Tuesday (Nov. 3). That's a boost of about 30%.

Menon and Kutryk are currently sharing the ISS with five other astronauts — NASA's Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins and cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Sergey Teteryatnikov.

Delaney, Kutryk, Teteryatnikov and Watkins arrived at the ISS on Oct. 1, on SpaceX's Crew-13 mission. Dubrov, Kikina and Menon got there in mid-July, aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft.
